newsitem.title: USA: W. House backs agressive use of spectrum auctions.
newsitem.headline: W. House backs agressive use of spectrum auctions.

text.p: The Clinton administration Monday advocated aggressive and flexible use of auctions to get the airwaves quickly in to the hands of companies that want to provide communications services.

The administration's position, spelled out in the annual Economic Report of the President, comes as Congress is set to focus on the use of spectrum auctions and as the Federal Communications Commission is split over spectrum policy.
While FCC Chairman Reed Hundt is an ardent supporter of aggressive and flexibile auctions, the agency's other three commissioners have not shared his zeal.
The administration's position also comes just days after it proposed in its fiscal 1998 budget to raise $36.1 billion over five years through airwave auctions.
In its report, the administration suggested that:
-- Auctions might not produce "efficient outcomes" if the government dicated ahead of time how companies should use the airwave slices being sold.
-- The government should commit to auctioning useful parts of the spectrum up front, rather than make the sale dependent on companies first developing technologies to make use of the spectrum.
-- The supply of available spectrum could be reduced if the government saw auctions primarily as revenue-raising devices.
